columns.description: `UEI`, `CAGE` or `NAME` - the key the owner's refusal was recorded against.
columns.name: identifier_type

columns.description: WITHHELD from publication. See the one-hop rule: SAM's public entity search resolves a UEI to a legal name and a street address.
columns.name: identifier

columns.description: The firm's Cedar surrogate. **The firm IS in the spine** as an individually Native-owned business; this row refuses a TRIBAL link, not the firm.
columns.name: firm_surrogate_entity_id

columns.description: WITHHELD from publication. Normalised firm name, present so a NAME-based resolver can honour the exclusion.
columns.name: firm_name_norm

columns.description: WITHHELD from publication. `core()` form of the firm name, same purpose.
columns.name: firm_name_core

columns.description: The spine entity the ruling refuses. Blank where the refusal is against ANY tribal, ANC or NHO owner rather than a named one.
columns.name: excluded_entity_id

columns.description: Canonical name of the refused entity. A tribe, ANC or NHO - a public body, so naming it raises none of the private-individual questions the firm's own name raises.
columns.name: excluded_entity_name

columns.description: Normalised form of the refused entity's name. **Present so the exclusion blocks the NAME path.** `resolve_entity` matches on names, so an exclusion recorded only against an identifier hands the same bad match straight back through the resolver.
columns.name: excluded_entity_name_norm

columns.description: `core()` form of the refused entity's name, same purpose.
columns.name: excluded_entity_name_core

columns.description: `PAIR` where a specific entity is refused, `ALL_TRIBAL_ANC_NHO_ENTITIES` where the refusal is general. **An exclusion is scoped to a (identifier, entity) PAIR, never applied as a blanket block on the identifier** - a blanket block suppresses a correct attribution somewhere else.
columns.name: exclusion_scope

columns.description: Always 1. The exclusion applies to identifier-keyed resolution.
columns.name: blocks_identifier_path

columns.description: Always 1. A consumer that honours only the identifier column has done half the job and will re-derive the defect through the resolver.
columns.name: blocks_name_path

columns.description: The outcome this exclusion came from. Always the refuse-tribal-link-affirm-individual-ownership outcome.
